metaDescription: Six electric and gas pressure washers compared by rated PSI, flow in GPM and cleaning units, so you can see past peak-pressure marketing to real cleaning power.
expertTake: The Westinghouse WPX3400 gas washer is the best pick for serious work because 2.6 GPM of flow cleans concrete far faster than any electric here. The Greenworks 3000 PSI brushless is the best electric for a homeowner who wants real power without an engine. If you only wash a car, a grill and some patio furniture, a compact 1.2 GPM electric is plenty and you should not pay for more.
introParagraphs: Pressure washers are sold on a single big number, but that number alone says very little. Cleaning power comes from pressure and water flow together, and the flow figure often decides how fast a job goes more than the pressure headline does.

The other trap is the difference between peak and rated output, especially on electric models. Learning to read those figures and match the machine to the surfaces you actually clean will protect you from overpaying and from damaging wood, siding or paint.

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3400 gas pressure washer, 3400 PSI 2.6 GPM
products.description:
A gas washer earns its place on flow. The WPX3400 pushes 2.6 GPM at 3400 PSI, which multiplies out to about 8,840 cleaning units, roughly three times the 2,400 or so that the best-rated electrics in this guide manage. That is the difference between spending ten minutes on a driveway and an hour.

The 212cc overhead-valve engine drives the pump directly, and a 25-foot abrasion-resistant hose, a metal gun and five quick-connect nozzles come in the box, along with an onboard soap tank. Compared with the Westinghouse WPX3400e, it moves more than twice the water, but it is louder, heavier, and needs fuel, oil and a pull start. Against the electric models it is the choice when time matters more than convenience.

Upkeep is the usual small-engine routine: change the oil, use fresh stabilized fuel, check the spark plug and air filter, and winterize the pump by draining it or running pump antifreeze through it so freezing does not crack it. Wear hearing and eye protection, since 3400 PSI can injure skin as well as strip paint, and never leave the trigger closed with the engine running because the pump heats up quickly.
products.bestFor: Driveways, decks and fences where speed on large areas matters more than quiet.
pros: 2.6 GPM flow cleans large areas fast
Soap tank and five nozzles included
cons: Loud, heavy, with a pull start

products.name: Greenworks 3000 PSI brushless electric pressure washer
products.description:
Greenworks aims this one squarely at the gas-versus-electric argument. A 14 amp TruBrushless motor generates 3000 PSI and up to 2.0 GPM, and the listing says the figures were verified by an independent lab, which is worth more than a raw peak claim because it ties the numbers to a test. JETTFLOW technology is described as delivering up to 50% more flow for reaching high areas and quick rinsing.

The 2.0 GPM maximum is still short of the WPX3400 gas machine's 2.6 GPM, and it is a max, not a sustained figure at full pressure, so read 3000 PSI times 2.0 GPM, or 6,000 cleaning units, as a ceiling. Against the Westinghouse WPX3400e, this one lists a higher flow, though the Westinghouse states a lower rated flow honestly.

Ownership is simple compared with gas: no oil, no fuel, no pull cord. An axial cam pump is common in electric machines and is not normally rebuildable, so protect it by never running it dry or with the trigger closed, draining it before a freeze and using clean water. Keep the extension cord short and heavy-gauge.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want near-gas power for driveways and decks without an engine.
pros: 3000 PSI and up to 2.0 GPM from a 14 amp motor
Output claims verified by an independent lab
Brushless motor runs cooler and quieter
No oil, fuel or pull cord
cons: 2.0 GPM is a maximum, not a sustained figure
Axial cam pump is not rebuildable

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3400e brushless electric pressure washer
products.description:
What makes this Westinghouse useful is that it states both sets of numbers. The 3400 PSI and 2.0 GPM figures are maximums at different settings, while the rated output of 3000 PSI at 1.1 GPM is what the machine delivers working under load. Multiply the rated figures and you get about 3,300 cleaning units, a realistic number for comparison.

That is why it sits between the compact electrics and the gas washer: more rated pressure than the 2000 PSI ePX3500, but only 1.1 GPM, so it blasts a small area hard rather than rinsing a large one quickly. The true brushless 120V motor and axial three-piston auto-stop pump are meant to be low maintenance, and the auto-stop shuts the motor when you release the trigger.

Treat the pump as a consumable that lasts if you look after it. Drain it before freezing weather, attach a hose with enough flow so it never starves, and use the soap tank at low pressure rather than through the high-pressure nozzle. The 25-foot hose and five quick-connect nozzles are included.
products.bestFor: Concentrated cleaning of stains on small to medium areas where pressure matters more than flow.
pros: States both max and rated output honestly
True brushless motor with auto-stop pump
cons: Rated flow of 1.1 GPM is slow on big areas
Needs a robust outlet and cord

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 compact electric pressure washer
products.description:
Here the engineering priority is portability: it stands 16.5 inches tall, weighs about 19 pounds and has four quick-lock wheels and anti-tipping features, so it rolls around a yard and stores in a closet. The rated output of 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM works out to about 2,400 cleaning units.

That puts it level with the Sun Joe SPX3000 in this guide and well below the 3000 PSI class, so it suits cars, patio furniture, grills, siding and light concrete, not heavy driveway grime. The 20-ounce onboard soap tank and 25-foot braided nylon hose are included. Against the Greenworks 2100, it is better documented on its rated output.

To keep it lasting, coil the braided hose loosely, store it where it will not freeze, and let the water drain before storing. Check the quick-connect o-rings and the hose ends for leaks each season. It is a sensible first machine, with no oil or fuel to manage.
products.bestFor: Cars, grills and patio furniture where light weight and easy storage matter.
pros: Four quick-lock wheels and anti-tip design
Clear rated output of 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM
cons: 2,400 cleaning units is modest for big areas
Max PSI figure is a peak, not working output

products.name: Sun Joe SPX3000 electric pressure washer
products.description:
Sun Joe labels this 2500 PSI max but lists the working figure as 2030 PSI at 1.2 GPM, a candid split that matches what the machine actually delivers. At about 2,436 cleaning units it is a near match for the Westinghouse ePX3500, with the main difference being the tools: a 34-inch stainless steel lance with solid brass fittings.

A longer lance means you stand upright instead of stooping, which matters on a long job such as a fence or deck. Five quick-connect tips cover everything from the 0-degree pencil jet to the soap nozzle. The corded 120V design suits small to medium jobs near an outlet.

Keep the nozzle tips away from wood and car paint at close range, and use the 25 or 40 degree tips for general rinsing. Replace the o-rings in the quick-connect when they weep, store it drained, and keep the extension cord rated for the load. It is a strong all-rounder for a modest budget.
products.bestFor: Fences, decks and general home use where a long lance and a candid rating help.
cons: Max label of 2500 PSI is a peak figure

products.name: Greenworks 2100 PSI electric pressure washer
products.description:
This is the plain-vanilla option: 2100 PSI at 1.2 GPM, push-button start and an integrated GFCI that cuts electrical power if a fault occurs. The maker positions it for medium-duty jobs such as fences and decking.

Multiply the headline figures and you get about 2,520 cleaning units at the labelled maximum, but the listing does not separate rated from peak output, so treat that as a ceiling. Compared with the Westinghouse ePX3500, it gives less detail on how the figures were derived, while the Westinghouse spells out rated output clearly.

It has no oil, spark plugs or air filter to maintain, which makes it an easy machine to own. Drain it after each use, avoid kinks in the hose and use fresh water. As a starter machine it handles cars, furniture and light siding well enough.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want a simple, no-maintenance washer for light work.
cons: Does not separate rated from peak output
1.2 GPM is slow on large areas

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cleaning units are pressure times flow, and flow often decides job speed. The gas WPX3400 at 3400 PSI and 2.6 GPM gives about 8,840 cleaning units, while the Westinghouse ePX3500 rated at 2000 PSI and 1.2 GPM gives about 2,400. Two machines with the same PSI can differ by a factor of two in speed.

Electric machines often print a peak pressure that applies at one setting and a peak flow that applies at another. The WPX3400e lists 3400 max PSI but 3000 rated PSI at 1.1 GPM, and the Sun Joe SPX3000 prints 2500 max but 2030 working. Compare the rated figures.

Electric tops out near 2000 to 3000 PSI at under 2 GPM, but starts at a button and needs no fuel. Gas runs up to about 2.8 GPM on consumer models. A 3400 PSI at 2.6 GPM pump needs an engine of about 11 horsepower in theory, so check engine size against claims.

Axial cam pumps are common on consumer machines, are economical and usually not rebuildable. Triplex plunger pumps are commercial grade and serviceable but cost more. The Westinghouse and Greenworks electrics use axial pumps, so protect them from dry running and freezing.

A 0-degree tip can damage almost anything, a 15 degree tip suits hard surfaces, and 25 and 40 degree tips suit general rinsing. A soap nozzle runs at low pressure. Match the tip to the surface, and keep tips away from wood and paint at close range.

Quick-connect fittings and hoses are common failure points. A braided hose like the one on the ePX3500 outlasts a plain one, and a stainless lance such as the Sun Joe's resists corrosion. Check that replacement hoses are easy to find.

specDecoder.meaning: Gallons per minute, the flow rate. It governs how quickly an area gets cleaned.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WPX3400 gas moves 2.6 GPM, while the ePX3500 rated flow is 1.2 GPM.

specDecoder.watchFor: Common on all the electrics here; never run it dry.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rated output
howWeEvaluated.description: We multiplied rated PSI by rated GPM wherever the maker gave both, preferring the honest split on the Westinghouse and Sun Joe. Peak figures were treated as ceilings. The lineup spans about 2,400 to 8,840 cleaning units.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source
howWeEvaluated.description: We split gas from electric because buyers weigh them differently. Gas wins on flow and speed, electric on convenience. We favoured machines that state their numbers plainly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pump and motor design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pump types, brushless motors and engine size from the spec sheets. Brushless motors run cooler, and a 212cc engine suits a 2.6 GPM pump. We read these claims against owner feedback patterns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accessories and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hoses, lances, tips and soap tanks, and weight from 19 pounds upward. A longer lance and a braided hose rated higher. Portability counted for small jobs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed upkeep: oil and fuel for gas, pump care and winterizing for all. Electric models with no engine scored higher for light use.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: The Greenworks, Westinghouse e-series and Sun Joe start at a button, run quieter and need no fuel. They max out near 3000 PSI at around 2 GPM or less, so big jobs take longer.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The WPX3400 delivers 2.6 GPM and about 8,840 cleaning units, cleaning large areas far faster. It is loud, heavy and needs fuel, oil and winterizing.

howToChoose.note: Choose electric for a typical home, and gas if you clean large concrete areas regularly.

howToChoose.subheading: For Vehicles and Soft Surfaces Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A machine you can run at low pressure with a 25 or 40 degree tip and a soap nozzle. Never use a 0-degree tip on paint or wood.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse ePX3500 and Greenworks 2100 are gentle enough with wide tips for cars and furniture. Avoid the WPX3400 gas for paint unless you use a wide tip well back.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean large concrete areas or want jobs done quickly. The WPX3400 gas or the Greenworks 3000 PSI pay back in time saved.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean cars, furniture and small patios. The ePX3500 or Greenworks 2100 are plenty.

maintenance.why: Water left in the pump can freeze and crack it. Drain it and run pump antifreeze through gas models.
A 212cc engine under load needs fresh oil to protect it.
Leaking fittings lose pressure and flow. Replace weeping o-rings.
Dry running overheats the pump in seconds. Open the water and purge air before pulling the trigger.
A clogged inlet screen starves the pump of water. Rinse it clean.

faq.q: What matters more, PSI or GPM?
faq.a: Both, but flow often decides how fast a job goes. Cleaning units, PSI times GPM, are a rough way to compare machines.

faq.q: Why is rated output lower than max?
faq.a: Max PSI and max GPM usually apply at different settings, so the machine cannot deliver both at once. Rated output is what you get working under load.

faq.q: Is gas always better than electric?
faq.a: Gas moves more water and cleans large areas faster, but electric starts at a button and needs no fuel. For a typical home, electric is plenty.

faq.q: Can a pressure washer damage my car or siding?
faq.a: Yes. Use a 25 or 40 degree tip, keep distance and never use a 0-degree tip on paint or wood. Wood, siding and vehicles want lower pressure.

faq.q: How long does an electric pressure washer last?
faq.a: The axial cam pump is the wear part. Protect it from dry running and freezing and it can last many seasons.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a pressure washer?
faq.a: Wear eye and hearing protection, and never point the nozzle at people or pets. High-pressure water can penetrate skin.
